# Hippius

> Hippius is a distributed cloud: encrypted file storage (Drive), S3-compatible object storage, a registry for AI models and containers (Hub), a CDN, and confidential compute (VMs, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes, GitHub Actions runners). One account pays for all of them. From a terminal, `hip` is the one command for the whole account. This file says how an agent gets set up, what each product is, and which file to open next.

Open only the file for the product you need. The long reference for the whole product, including the S3 manual, is [llms-full.txt](https://docs.hippius.com/llms-full.txt)

## If you can run commands, start with hip

`hip` is the Hippius command line, written for coding agents and for people. It covers everything the console and the account API do: accounts, projects and teams, the balance and the plans, S3 buckets and tokens, Hub, confidential VMs, managed Kubernetes and PostgreSQL, GitHub Actions runners, CDN zones and WAF, the private network, and support tickets. Use it instead of calling https://api.hippius.com by hand: it carries the token, the account header, the confirmations, and one JSON error shape. It moves no data; S3 objects go through any S3 client, Hub blobs through `hippius-hub`.

1. Install, no root, macOS and Linux: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/thenervelab/hippius-cli/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh` (or `brew install thenervelab/tap/hip`; or `pip install hippius` from 1.0.0). Then `hip version`.
2. Log in once with the token the user gives you. The user copies it from https://console.hippius.com/dashboard/settings; an agent cannot create the account or sign in. Run `hip auth login --token-file -`, paste the token, press Enter, then Ctrl-D; or `hip auth login --token-file <path>`. The token never goes in argv, and never into the chat. `hip auth status` confirms it. For one run without storing it, set `HIPPIUS_TOKEN`.
3. Learn it from the binary: `hip schema` prints every command with its effect, flags, confirmation, guards, and every error code, as JSON, with no network; then `hip <command> --help`.

Three commands:

    hip account get
    hip billing balance
    hip s3 buckets create photos --dry-run

The contract, in five lines:

- On a pipe, or with `CI` or `AI_AGENT=1`, output is JSON: the resource itself, or a list as `{"items":[...],"next_page_token":null}`; `--json` forces it.
- A failure is one JSON object on stderr, `{"error":{"code":...,"message":...,"hint":...,"retryable":...,"side_effects":...}}`; branch on `code`.
- Exit 0 is success (a dry run included), 1 the API or the runtime failed, 2 the invocation must change and nothing was sent.
- A command that spends, deletes, revokes, rotates, or cancels needs `--yes`; a secret in the answer needs `--reveal`; `--dry-run` prints the requests and sends nothing. `CI` and `AI_AGENT` never confirm on their own.
- `hip api GET /accounts/` reaches any endpoint hip has no command for, with the same rules.

Playbook: [hip for agents](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents), also raw at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-cli/main/docs/agents.md. Pages: [Get started](https://docs.hippius.com/cli), [Examples](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/examples), [Command reference](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/commands). Source: https://github.com/thenervelab/hippius-cli

## Which file to open

| Want to | Open |
|---|---|
| Manage the account, billing, plans, S3 buckets and keys, Hub, compute, Kubernetes, databases, runners, CDN, the private network, or support from a terminal or an agent | [hip](https://docs.hippius.com/cli) and [hip for agents](https://docs.hippius.com/cli/agents); install and log in as above, then `hip schema` |
| Store or fetch files from code, rclone, or a backup tool | [hippius-s3 llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-s3/staging/llms.txt) |
| Store encrypted files in the browser (Drive) | [Drive guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/drive) |
| Publish or pull a model or a container image | [hippius-hub llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-hub/main/llms.txt); the namespace, plan, and CI keys are also `hip hub` |
| Sync folders on a computer | [hippius-desktop llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-desktop/staging/llms.txt) |
| Work in a shared drive | A Drive someone else owns and invited you into. They pay for the storage. It shows in the console under Storage after the invite. |
| Give a coding agent shared memory | [hippius-mem llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-mem/main/llms.txt) |
| Script Drive with encryption on the client | [hippius-drive-sdk llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/hippius-drive-sdk/main/llms.txt) |
| Sign up, pay, get an API token, or manage Drive and S3 keys in the browser | [Console getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/getting-started) |
| Use Drive on an Android phone | [Mobile getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/mobile/getting-started) |
| Run a VM, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes or GitHub Actions runners (Compute) | `hip compute`, and the [Compute guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute) |
| Serve an S3 bucket through the CDN (zones on <zone>.c.hipcdn.net or your own domain; FR $0.010/GB, AU $0.060/GB, $0.002 per 10,000 requests, $1/month per custom domain) | `hip cdn`, and the [CDN guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/cdn) |
| Filter requests to a CDN zone with a WAF: custom rules, rate limits, IP/ASN/country lists (every zone, Security tab; Standard $5, Advanced $20 per zone per month) | `hip cdn waf`, and the [CDN guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/cdn) |
| Read compute, CDN, S3, Drive and Hub prices without an account (`hip compute public-prices`, `hip s3 plans`, or GET https://api.hippius.com/api/compute/public-prices/, no auth), or sign users in with their 12-word access key from your own app | [Management API](https://docs.hippius.com/use/api), which links the Public Price API and Access Key Sign-In API pages |
| Let team members use your compute, S3 and CDN, or work in an account you were invited to (shared accounts) | `hip account list`, `hip account use <account_id>`, and the [Shared accounts guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/team) |
| Run a storage miner | [Miner guide](https://docs.hippius.com/earn/arion/running-miner) and [arion llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenervelab/arion/main/llms.txt) |
| Run a validator | [Validator guide](https://docs.hippius.com/earn/installing-validator) |

## Account, sign-in, and paying

Full console guide: [Console getting started](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/getting-started)
Billing: [Billing guide](https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing)

- One account covers the console, the desktop app, the mobile app, and `hip`. Sign-in is Google, GitHub, Apple, or an existing 12-word access key. There is no email and password sign-in.
- An agent cannot create the account or sign in. That happens in the user's browser or app. The agent gets the API token from the user and stores it with `hip auth login --token-file -`.
- A 12-word access key creates a wallet-only account. It has no real email address, so it gets no lifecycle mail. Drive has no free plan: subscribe before the first upload. S3 and Hub work the same as on any other account.
- S3 endpoint is https://s3.hippius.com only. Keys (the access key id starts with `hip_`) are created with `hip s3 tokens create --kind master --reveal --yes`, or on the console S3 page: https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/s3. `hip s3 configure` writes an AWS CLI profile from one.
- The API token for Hub, the account API, and `hip` is on console Settings: https://console.hippius.com/dashboard/settings
- Hub has a second credential, the registry robot login, created when the namespace is provisioned (`hip hub namespace provision --reveal --yes`, or `hippius-hub`).
- Drive encryption uses an unlock password and a 12-word recovery seed. Never ask the user to paste either into chat.
- 1 USDC adds one dollar to your balance. Topping up fills the balance. It does not add storage. Subscribe to a plan for that. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing
- Top up on Billing in one of five ways. Card, through Stripe, from $10 to $10,000, or a monthly auto reload (`hip billing top-up --amount 10 --method card --yes` prints the checkout URL; `hip billing auto-reload update`). Bitcoin, on-chain or Lightning, from $20 to $100,000. Lightning lands in seconds; on-chain after one confirmation. USDC on Base from a browser wallet, from $5 to $10,000; 1 USDC adds one dollar to your balance. TAO, from a connected wallet or by sending to the TAO deposit address (Manually tab), at least $20 per transfer; never send TAO to the Hippius account address, which is not credited. A transfer cannot be reversed. hAlpha (Hippius native token), on the Hippius tab: credits = hAlpha × the on-chain hAlpha price, 1% slippage protection by default, final on chain with no refund. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/billing
- An agent with enough balance subscribes without a browser: `hip drive subscription subscribe --plan solo --yes` (codes `solo` Starter, `duo` Plus, `max`, `scale`; `--period monthly|annual`), `hip s3 subscription subscribe --plan pro --yes` (codes `pro`, `business`, `enterprise`), `hip hub subscription subscribe --plan Builder --yes` (names Free, Builder, Pro, Team; paid from the balance only; a second paid plan needs `--replace`). Run each with `--dry-run` first. The plan lists are `hip drive plans`, `hip s3 plans`, `hip hub plans`, with no token. Card checkout is a browser; do not send a funded agent there.
- Google, GitHub, and Apple accounts include the Free Drive Plan (10 GB). S3 starts on pay as you go at $6 per TB per month, and a plan is optional.
- Plan prices, monthly, from the balance (always current in the catalogs): Drive Free 10 GB $0, Starter 500 GB $4, Plus 2 TB $7, Max 10 TB $22, Scale 25 TB $50 (Max and Scale bill storage above the plan hourly, $2.20 and $2.00 per TB per month, up to a storage cap that defaults to twice the plan). S3 Pro 10 TB $53, Business 50 TB $245, Enterprise 100 TB $465 (pay as you go otherwise: $6 per TB per month). Hub Free $0, Builder $5, Pro $19, Team $99.
- Shared accounts: an owner invites members by email, with Viewer, Operator or Admin access per product (VMs, databases, Kubernetes, runners, S3, CDN). The owner pays and the owner's quotas apply. Drive is not included. `hip account list` shows the accounts a token can act in; `hip account use <account_id>` or `--account <account_id>` acts in one. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/team
- Open a support ticket: `hip support tickets create --subject <text> --body-file <path> --yes`.

Hub Free plan: creating a namespace requires a balance of at least $10, a spam check. A zero balance is refused. The plan price stays zero. Top up, then provision. https://docs.hippius.com/use/console/hub

## Only if hip does not cover it: hip api, or the raw API

`hip api <METHOD> <PATH>` calls any endpoint of https://api.hippius.com with the same token, account header, confirmations, guards, and error object as every command: `hip api GET /accounts/`, `hip api POST /support/tickets/ --body-file ticket.json --yes`. The OpenAPI spec is https://api.hippius.com/swagger.json. Without hip: header `Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN`, plus `X-Hippius-Account: acct_...` for a shared account (ids from GET https://api.hippius.com/api/accounts/). Subscribe routes: POST https://api.hippius.com/api/drive/subscription/ with `{"plan":"solo","period":"monthly","payment":"credits"}`; POST https://api.hippius.com/api/s3/subscription/ with `{"plan":"pro","rail":"credits"}`; GET https://api.hippius.com/api/registry/plans/ then POST https://api.hippius.com/api/registry/subscribe/ with `{"plan_id": 2}` (the API requires `plan_id`, not a name; Builder is id 2). 201 if the balance covers the plan. Support: POST https://api.hippius.com/api/support/tickets/ with subject, priority, category, and description. Send your own User-Agent: some default ones (Python urllib) are blocked with 403 error 1010.

## Deprecated

`hipc`, the IPFS-era command line that the hippius-cli repository held before `hip`, `homebrew-tap`'s `hipc` formula, `hippius-sdk`, `hippius-sdk-ts`, `hippius-sdk-rust`, `hippius-rust-sdk`, `hippius-sync-engine`, `hippius-storage-miner`, the storage commands of the Python package `hippius` up to 0.2.77, and anything else IPFS-related, are deprecated. Hippius switched from IPFS to Arion. https://docs.hippius.com/cli/usage

Chain registration still installs the Python package `hippius` (pin `hippius==0.2.77`; from 1.0.0 the name ships `hip`): https://docs.hippius.com/earn/register-in-blockchain

## Compute

Confidential VMs on AMD SEV-SNP, managed PostgreSQL, managed Kubernetes and GitHub Actions runners, open to every account. Metered per second (one-minute minimum per VM and public IPv4), charged hourly on the Hippius chain from the account balance. A VM is billed running or stopped until it is deleted. A launch needs a balance covering 24 hours of the account's compute plus the launch, and quotas apply: new accounts start on the Starter tier and move up automatically with their charged usage.

From a terminal: `hip compute flavors`, `hip compute regions`, `hip compute quota`, `hip compute ssh-keys create --name laptop --public-key-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --yes`, then `hip compute vms create --flavor small --name web-1 --ssh-key-id <key_id> --dry-run` and the same with `--yes`; `hip compute vms get <vm_id>` follows it to `running`; `hip compute public-ip create <vm_id> --yes` adds an IPv4, `hip compute firewall update` opens ports. Databases are `hip compute databases`, Kubernetes `hip compute kubernetes`, runners `hip compute runners`. `hip compute prices` and `hip compute public-prices` are the live price list.

Prices per 730-hour month, on the default NVMe OS disk: vCPU $18, memory $2.50/GB, disk $0.10/GB. Small (1 vCPU, 4 GB, 40 GB) is $32 a month ($0.0438/h), Medium $64, Large $128, X-Large $256, 2X-Large $512, 4X-Large $1024. The OS disk tier is chosen at launch and fixed: SSD (disk $0.06/GB, Small $27.60, Medium $55.20, Large $110.40) or HDD, a slow tier for dev and test offered up to Large (disk $0.03/GB, Small $17.16, Medium $34.32, Large $68.64). Dedicated disks (whole physical disks for one VM, up to 8, at least 1,000 GiB each; the VM is then pinned: no backups, migration or failover): $2.50 HDD, $5 SSD, $8 NVMe per TiB-month. Public IPv4 $0.005/h (~$3.65/month). VM backups $6 per TB-month. Outbound bandwidth is metered per region and not charged today; inbound is free. Managed databases cost their VMs plus 25%; Kubernetes costs its VMs plus $15 per cluster per month. The live price list wins: https://console.hippius.com/dashboard/billing/compute#prices

- Overview (quotas, the 24-hour balance requirement, billing): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute
- Create a VM and connect over SSH or from the browser: https://docs.hippius.com/use/virtual-machines
- Public IPv4, firewall rules and published ports: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/networking
- Resize a VM (vCPU and memory; the disk is kept): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/resize
- VM backups and restore: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-backups
- Dedicated disks (whole physical HDD/SSD/NVMe disks, exact tier, pinned VM, own quota): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/dedicated-disks
- VM failover: if a VM's server dies, the VM restarts on another server in the same region from its latest backup, keeping its IP and NetBird address; data since that backup is lost. Automatic failover is opt-in per VM, at creation (switch under Automatic backups; API `"failover_mode": "auto"` with `backup_interval_s`) or later in the Backups panel. Offered in France only today. Active after the first full backup: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-failover
- Placement groups: VMs of one account in the same group (`placement_group` at creation, 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9, -) are never on the same server. A different server is not a different datacenter. Fixed at creation: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/vm-failover#placement-groups
- Compute API, only without hip: base https://api.hippius.com/api, header `Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN` (plus `X-Hippius-Account: acct_...` for a shared account). Full OpenAPI spec: https://api.hippius.com/swagger.json. Create a VM with POST /api/compute/vms/ `{"name":"web-1","flavor":"small","region":"FR","ssh_key_ids":[123]}` (keys from GET /api/ssh-keys/), then poll GET /api/compute/vms/<vm_id>/ until `status` is `running` and, with a public IPv4, `network_ready` is `true`, then SSH to the public IP (or to `netbird_ip` over NetBird). `status` is the lifecycle (billed while `running`, stopped included), `power_state` is on/off: https://docs.hippius.com/use/api#compute-api
- Managed PostgreSQL 16/17/18 (one-time credentials, TLS, backups to your S3, restore, HA failover): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/databases
- Managed Kubernetes clusters (cluster key, kubeconfig, API access): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes
- Kubernetes worker pools and signed node operations: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes-worker-pools
- Kubernetes backups (etcd snapshots, Velero, restore with rclone): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/kubernetes-backups
- GitHub Actions runners (`runs-on: hippius-small|medium|large`, `-ssd` for the cheaper SSD tier; spend per day, repository, size and workflow, compared with GitHub-hosted runners): https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/runners
- Compute prices, management fees, quotas and unpaid balance: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/billing
- Refusals and troubleshooting: https://docs.hippius.com/use/compute/troubleshooting

The Kubernetes cluster key is generated in the user's browser, and database credentials are returned once at creation (`hip compute databases create --reveal --yes` writes them to files only the user can read); never ask the user to paste either into chat.
